## Constitution Established

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-11-16 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-16

**Bump rationale**: The existing `.specify/memory/constitution.md` was an unpopulated scaffold — every placeholder was still bracketed and no principle had been defined. This is therefore an initial ratification at 1.0.0, not an amendment to a prior governing version.

**Principles ratified** (four, matching your input exactly — the template's fifth principle slot was removed):

| # | Principle | Core enforceable rule |
|---|---|---|
| I | Standard Library Only | No third-party imports in runtime code; pytest exempt but may not be imported by runtime modules |
| II | Fail Loudly | Specific diagnostic + non-zero exit (CLI) or raised exception (library); no defaulting, coercing, or swallowing |
| III | Every Requirement Is Testable (NON-NEGOTIABLE) | Each functional requirement maps to ≥1 pytest test, mapping made explicit; untested requirement = unimplemented |
| IV | Simplicity | Smallest design meeting the spec; no speculative generality; deviations justified in writing |

I turned each principle into something a reviewer can check rather than interpret. Two drafting decisions worth your attention:

- **Principle I** — I carved out an explicit exemption for pytest and other dev tooling, since Principle III mandates pytest and a literal "no third-party dependencies" reading would contradict it. The exemption is scoped: dev tools must never be imported by runtime code.
- **Principle III** — I extended it so the error paths required by Principle II are themselves testable requirements, with tests asserting message content and exit status. Without that, "fail loudly" would have been the one principle with no enforcement mechanism.

I also added a **Development Workflow & Quality Gates** section translating the four principles into five concrete review gates, and marked gates 1–4 as objectively verifiable and non-waivable, with gate 5 (simplicity) explicitly flagged as a judgment call.
